abstract: This paper examines COVID-19′s impact on the agglomeration economies in service industries, using administrative firm registration and deregistration records from Zhejiang province, China. Results indicate that new firms became less likely to cluster within the same industry after the onset of COVID-19, particularly in prime services and industries better suited to remote work. Localization effects continued to attenuate rapidly with distance after COVID-19. However, these effects weakened at shorter distances, while spillovers at longer distances remained unchanged or became stronger, resulting in a flatter attenuation slope. These findings reveal a weakening of proximity-based advantages, which has reshaped firms’ location decisions.

abstract: The utilization of automation in recent decades and its displacement effect on routine tasks is well documented, but its further influence on market structure has not been studied. In this paper, we analyze micro panel data for manufacturing in China from 2013-2020 and suggest how the adoption of automation influences markup divergence through routine tasks. We find that (i) automation raises markups for firms; (ii) firms contain more routine tasks benefit more from automation for their markups; (iii) the difference in markups between high and low markup firms increases because high markup firms which already perform better can import more automation machines to substitute workers doing routine tasks. The results still hold after mitigating endogeneity and implementing a series of robustness tests.

abstract: Using a novel setting, we examine auditors’ responses to public warnings of audit risk and whether their nonresponses are associated with auditor and client characteristics. We focus on 243 short-selling campaigns from 2006 to 2020 in which short sellers make public, credible allegations of audit-related issues against listed companies. Of those companies’ auditors, 48.3% do not take any observable actions in terms of raising audit fees substantially, terminating the engagement, issuing going concern opinions, or reporting internal control weaknesses in the year after the short sellers’ allegations. We further find that longer auditor–client tenure is the factor most consistently associated with auditors’ nonresponse to public warnings of audit risk, a pattern arguably consistent with impaired independence. Additional analyses show that the litigation and reputation costs of auditors’ inactions are minimal, further reducing auditors’ incentives for responses.
title: Auditors’ (non)responses to public warnings of audit risk: evidence from short-selling campaigns

abstract: Postal and courier services have become an important channel for drug trafficking worldwide. This study examines the impact of digital monitoring of mail on drug use. Based on the universe of drug arrest records in a populous province in China, the difference-in-differences analysis reveals that, after the implementation of real-identity mailing (RIM) in 2017, the number of punished drug users decreased by 5.8% in townships with any courier service points. This effect persists for at least 1 year. The number of first-time users diminishes, while the number of addicted users remains constant. These suggest that strengthening the regulation of postal and courier services may be a cost-effective approach to drug control, and courier service platforms and government could collaborate to solve public health challenges and improve social welfare.

abstract: The quality of investors’ information across different horizons has real effects. When managers care about the effect of investment on their stock price, a decline in the informativeness of investors’ signals about long-term cash flows leads firms with long-term projects to cut investment more than firms with short-term projects. Using a novel, hand-collected measure of project horizons, we confirm this hypothesis: relative to firms with short-term projects, the investment of firms with long-term projects decreases by 3.7% following a 1-standard-deviation drop in the quality of investors’ long-term information. This effect becomes larger when managers prioritize current stock prices. (JEL D84, G14, G17, M41).
title: The Horizon of Investors’ Information and Corporate Investment

abstract: A central puzzle in the social sciences is that, despite high and rising inequality, democracies consistently under-deliver redistributive policies. Research in economics and political science has documented one explanation for this puzzle: beliefs about the extent of inequality are polarized along ideological lines, with liberals believing there to be more inequality than conservatives. We decompose this ideological divide in inequality perceptions into two sources: the decision threshold applied by liberals and conservatives when classifying possible instances of inequality (‘criterion’) and their tendency to perceive inequality to begin with (‘sensitivity’). Across six studies (N = 2734), we find that liberals consistently report seeing more inequality than conservatives when exposed to identical stimuli. A formal signal detection decomposition reveals ideological differences in both the discriminability of inequality signals (‘sensitivity’) and the threshold applied when classifying them (‘criterion’). The ideological gap in perceived inequality disappears when stimuli depict inequality unambiguously— that is, when the signal is strong enough to clear even the strictest decision thresholds. Notably, we find that perceived inequality is associated with fairness concerns and support for redistributive policies above and beyond ideological orientation. These findings suggest that the everyday settings in which people encounter instances of social inequality are themselves likely to produce consequential differences in beliefs about the extent of inequality.
journal: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization
title: Decomposing the ideological divide in perceptions of inequality: a signal detection approach

abstract: This paper studies the effect of regional trade agreements on firms’ exports using detailed information on the content of trade agreements and firm-level exports for 31 developing countries between 2000 and 2020. Moving from shallow to deep trade agreements—-i.e. agreements that regulate border and behind-the-border policies—-boosts firms’ exports, on average, by 3.6 percent. This effect is stronger for large firms and firms involved in global value chains and (weakly) negative for small firms, documenting a reallocation of exports toward larger exporters associated with deeper agreements—consistent with models of trade with heterogeneous firms—with significant welfare consequences for signatory countries. An Instrumental Variable strategy and a battery of robustness tests confirm the causal interpretation of the results.
title: Deep trade agreements and heterogeneous firms’ exports

abstract: 城乡融合发展是中国式现代化的必然要求，对于推进乡村全面振兴、实现共同富裕具有重要意义。现有相关研究多局限于经济学、社会学、管理学等单一学科视角，对城乡复合生态系统的整体属性关注不足，生态维度的研究存在明显短板，难以系统解释城乡生态割裂的深层机理与破解路径。本文以共生理论、生态位理论、稳定性理论、演替理论、平衡理论这五大生态学理论为支撑，构建城乡融合发展的递进式分析框架，阐释了城乡复合生态系统从失衡走向共生、从低级向高级演化的内在机理。在此基础上，结合生态学核心原理，从筑牢城乡融合发展的生态基底、构建差异化发展格局、提升系统抗风险能力、推动阶梯式演进、实现公平共享五个维度，提出了具有可操作性的实践策略，涵盖了生态空间管控、物质循环利用、功能冗余保障、产业梯度升级、要素双向流动、公共服务均等化及生态保护补偿机制等重点领域。本文突破传统研究范式，将生态学理论体系有机融入城乡融合发展研究之中，拓展生态规律与城乡关系系统性结合的研究视角，以期为破解城乡二元结构、修复城乡生态割裂、构建城乡生态共生体系提供理论支撑与实践参考，对推进人与自然和谐共生的中国式现代化具有重要价值。

abstract: 在中国区域和城乡收入差距仍然较大的情况下，核心劳动年龄群体的流动却在快速下降，传统经济模型遭遇解释困境。本文揭示子女升学压力已成为束缚劳动力流动的一个重要因素。结合当前教育竞争加剧的现实背景，本文构建包含子女升学压力的家庭流动决策模型，运用2005－2015年全国人口普查抽样微观数据与2023年中国住户收入调查（CHIP）数据，借助工具变量法检验子女升学压力对劳动力流动的影响及其机制。研究发现，子女升学压力会显著抑制劳动力流动，且对升学压力更大、教育期望更高以及社会经济资源相对有限的家庭影响更为突出。机制分析表明，子女升学压力迫使父母增加照料时间，同时因担心留守子女发展而承受较高的心理成本，从而削弱了流动意愿。进一步讨论显示，子女升学压力更多抑制远距离跨省流动，但降低迁入地落户门槛可有效缓解这一负向效应。本文揭示了教育竞争对劳动力流动的梗阻效应，应通过提升随迁子女教育保障水平、缩小区域教育资源差距、增强职业教育吸引力，助推劳动力要素高效配置。

abstract: 深化县域医疗卫生服务体系改革、开展县域医疗卫生共同体建设，既是落实健康中国战略的重要举措，也是减轻居民就医负担的有效途径。本文利用2014－2022年中国家庭追踪调查（CFPS）数据，运用交错双重差分法，考察县域医疗卫生共同体建设对居民就医负担的影响及其作用机制。研究发现，县域医疗卫生共同体建设显著减少了居民自付医疗费用，且减负效应主要集中于高额自付医疗费用群体；机制分析表明，县域医疗卫生共同体建设通过提升医疗服务质量和降低居民患病风险两条路径减轻居民就医负担；异质性分析显示，县域医疗卫生共同体建设对基期首诊机构选择为高层级医疗机构和基期健康状况较差居民的就医负担减轻效应更为显著，而参与不同医保类型的居民之间的就医负担减轻效应未表现出显著差异。本文从减轻居民就医负担的角度揭示了县域医疗卫生共同体建设的政策效应及其作用机制，以期为全面推进县域医疗卫生共同体建设、深入实施健康中国战略提供经验证据和政策启示。

abstract: 本文立足中国“大国小农”的基本国情农情与农业现代化实践，着眼农业新质生产力发展的时代背景，聚焦农业的自然依赖性及其分工约束问题，对“斯密判断”所揭示的农业分工受限这一经典命题进行重新审视。研究表明，农业新质生产力以生物技术、数字技术和智能装备等前沿技术的突破为基础，经由技术革命、要素重构与组织创新三重路径，系统性地弱化农业在空间、时间与过程上的自然依赖性，从而为打破传统的“自然－小农”双重锁定结构提供物质基础和技术条件。这一弱化自然依赖性的生产力质变，推动农业生产关系在经营模式、产权结构、产业形态与治理体系四个维度发生深刻重构，并由此形成以服务规模化和数字网络化赋能小农为特征的中国农业现代化路径。本文提出的“自然依赖性弱化”命题及其分析框架，为理解农业生产关系重构提供了新的理论视角，也为中国农业现代化实践提供了学理依据与政策启示。

abstract: 农产品期货交易形成的价格信号能够汇集并传递分散于不同地区的市场信息，为缓解区域间信息不对称创造条件。本文使用中国89家大型农副产品批发市场的100余万条日度价格数据，采用动态价格法测算11种农产品在城市配对层面的季度市场一体化指标，并将农产品期货上市视为准自然实验，采用双重差分法考察其对现货市场一体化的影响。研究发现：第一，农产品期货上市提高了对应农产品的现货市场一体化水平，促进信息整合与加快信息传导是其重要作用机制。第二，农产品期货市场流动性的改善和套期保值交易活跃度的提高均有助于促进现货市场一体化。第三，在地理距离较远的城市之间，农产品期货上市与高铁连通具有协同促进现货市场一体化的作用。本文研究结论有助于理解期货市场对农产品区域间价格差异的影响，并为推进全国统一大市场建设提供经验证据。

abstract: 本文以中国、美国、巴西、阿根廷和加拿大五国大豆市场为样本，采用分位数时频溢出指数方法，系统测度主要贸易伙伴国与中国大豆市场间的价格溢出效应，进而实证探究气候风险对大豆价格跨境溢出的影响及作用渠道。研究发现：第一，主要贸易伙伴国与中国大豆市场间存在较强的价格溢出效应；正常状态下的总溢出水平低于极端状态，短期溢出强于长期溢出。第二，大豆价格跨境溢出网络中的主导国随市场状态动态调整。第三，无论是在何种市场状态和时间频率下，中国始终是溢出效应的净输入方。第四，贸易伙伴国气候风险上升会加剧其对中国大豆市场的价格溢出效应。其中，气候物理风险的影响具有常态化趋势，主要通过国际贸易渠道传导；气候转型风险的影响更多反映在极端市场状态下，主要通过情绪传染渠道传导。第五，气候风险对大豆价格跨境溢出的影响具有显著的区域异质性，南美国家为价格极端下跌状态下气候物理风险向中国长期传导的核心来源地；北美国家既主导了气候物理风险对中国大豆价格的常态化传导，也是价格极端上涨状态下气候转型风险向中国长期传导的核心来源地。本文研究为防范外部气候风险冲击、维护国内大豆市场稳定以及保障国家粮食安全提供了有益启示。

abstract: 政策性农业信贷担保作为破解农村融资约束的重要政策工具，对粮食生产中的环境友好、增产增收具有重要的赋能作用。本文以2015年起中国各地级市逐步设立政策性农业信贷担保分支机构作为政策冲击，运用多时期双重差分模型考察政策性农业信贷担保对粮食可持续生产能力的影响及作用机制。研究表明：政策性农业信贷担保对粮食可持续生产能力具有显著的提升作用。促进信贷供给下沉和推动农业资本深化是两个重要的影响机制。不同于政策性农业信贷担保只要释放效能便会带动信贷供给下沉的作用逻辑，随着时间的推移，政策性农业信贷担保对粮食生产中农业资本深化的推动作用呈逐渐减弱趋势，这主要源于“去担保化”的影响。此外，政策性农业信贷担保更有助于提高粮食主产区、财政涉农支持程度低和数字金融水平低的地区的粮食可持续生产能力。本文建议，提高担保的精准覆盖度与服务可得性，推动“去担保化”平稳过渡并构建长效服务机制，实施区域差异化支持政策，进而推动农业信贷担保政策高效落地。

abstract: 农村集体经济组织在传统经营中面临市场竞争能力弱、治理不完善等诸多问题，设立公司被视为盘活集体资源、发展新型农村集体经济的重要举措。然而，实践中农村集体经济组织如何成功设立公司仍是有待研究的重要问题。本文采用多案例研究方法，选取四个典型村庄，深入探究农村集体经济组织设立公司的差异化路径及其选择依据。研究发现，基于参与主体的不同，实践中主要形成了单村独立运营、多村抱团、村企合作以及与自然人合资四条有效路径。不同路径具有各自的适用条件：单村独立运营适用于具备潜在资源优势且内部组织有力的村庄；多村抱团适用于地域相邻、具备一定资源且上级政府能够有效统筹的村庄集群；村企合作适用于开发潜力较大但缺乏资本与运营能力的村庄；与自然人合资则适用于具备资源优势、拟开发中小型项目的村庄。同时，各条路径在实践中均面临一定的潜在风险。本文拓展了产权理论的研究边界，为发展壮大新型农村集体经济、推进乡村振兴与实现共同富裕提供了理论参考和路径选择。

abstract: 盘活农村集体经营性资产，是发展壮大新型农村集体经济和扎实推进乡村全面振兴的重要抓手。本文基于2020－2022年中国土地经济调查数据，从利益联结视角出发，分析村庄产业融合对村集体经营性资产价值实现的影响及其作用机制，并识别风险治理的边界条件。研究表明：第一，村庄产业融合显著促进了村集体经营性资产价值实现，主要体现在内部融合型与多功能拓展型两种产业融合模式的发展上。第二，村庄产业融合通过土地集中流转、强化农户集体行动、吸引社会资本投资以及建立利益联结共享机制等方式促进村集体经营性资产价值实现。第三，有效契约和组织监管作为风险治理的关键边界条件，有助于防范村庄产业融合过程中的契约风险，保障村集体经营性资产价值实现的安全性与稳定性。第四，上述效应在基础设施更加完善、治理能力更强的村庄中更为显著；相较于单一的“合作社”或“龙头企业”模式，“合作社+龙头企业”模式是实现村集体经营性资产价值的更优组织形式。上述结论为推进农村产业融合发展，进而盘活农村集体经营性资产、壮大新型农村集体经济提供了微观证据与决策参考。

abstract: Can artificial intelligence extend students’ analytical capabilities without displacing their independent judgement? This column reports on a pilot study in a graduate seminar investigating weaknesses in European integration. An ‘AI-enriched contract’ required three elements for students’ presentations: an independent conceptualisation before AI use, an AI-assisted presentation, and a transparency statement. AI-tools accelerated routine execution, widened methodological ambition, and enabled exploration. Students also documented verification, rejected inappropriate suggestions and fabricated quotations, and retained responsibility for organisation and interpretation of findings. While the pilot offers qualified support for AI as a workmate rather than a master, several caveats apply.
title: AI – Master and Commander: Lessons from graduate student projects and the need for an AI-enriched contract

abstract: Official statistics are getting harder to collect and can arrive late. This column uses generative AI to read managers’ economic outlooks from more than 120,000 corporate earnings calls in the US. The resulting score predicts GDP, employment, and wages beyond the next quarter and carries information that professional forecasters do not.
authors: Manish Jha, Jialin Qian, Michael Weber, Baozhong Yang
title: Reading the economy from earnings calls with generative AI

abstract: Despite climate-mitigation commitments in the global South, an implementation gap constrains sustainable agricultural development in South Africa. This study examines government extension practitioners' perceptions of climate-aligned practices to identify the institutional factors driving this divide. A qualitative content analysis of 1775 thematic segments from focus groups with 52 extension officers across eight provinces in 2025 reveals deep institutional misalignment. Only 10.7% of coded segments explicitly framed agriculture as a mitigation strategy, while 35.8% prioritize economic optimization and livelihood conservation. Provincial focus on climate mitigation ranges from 20.3% in Mpumalanga to 4.7% in Gauteng. Crucially, land tenure insecurity emerges as a foundational structural constraint that contributes to this misalignment by discouraging long-term climate investment. While national mandates conceptualize mitigation through global carbon accounting, local extension systems prioritize immediate economic survival. Therefore, achieving national targets requires reforming communal land governance alongside extension mandates, rather than merely introducing technical solutions. The study demonstrates that land governance reform is a prerequisite, rather than a complementary measure, for effective climate policy implementation. It advances frameworks that leverage smart technologies for carbon measurement, youth-led data management, and carbon credits, reframing mitigation as a viable economic strategy for a sustainable, low-carbon future.
title: Transitioning to low-carbon agriculture: Institutional misalignment and constraints in South Africa’s extension systems

abstract: Urbanization and associated land use and land cover (LULC) change are major drivers of surface transformation with significant implications for climate impacts. The conversion of vegetated and permeable landscapes into built-up areas alters energy balance, disrupts carbon and hydrological cycles, and intensifies heat exposure. However, existing studies remain fragmented, with most studies examining urbanization, LULC change, or climate impacts separately, without fully integrating them into a unified framework. To address this gap, this study provides a comprehensive global synthesis of the interactions among urbanization, LULC change, and climate impacts. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, the review synthesizes 116 peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and 2024 that examine urban expansion, LULC transitions, and climate-related outcomes. The results show that urban growth is predominantly driven by peri-urban expansion, with the conversion of vegetated land to impervious surfaces emerging as the dominant land transition. The reviewed studies further indicate that the climate impacts of urbanization and associated LULC change extend beyond rising land surface temperatures to include changes in energy balance, hydrological processes, and carbon dynamics. The findings have important implications for integrated land-use planning and zoning, compact urban development, urban greening, and coordinated planning aimed at moderating the climatic impacts of urban expansion. However, existing planning responses may remain insufficient in many rapidly urbanizing contexts, highlighting the need for stronger implementation and better coordination to support climate-resilient and sustainable urban development.
title: Understanding interactions among urbanization, land use and land cover change, and climate impacts: Implications for climate-resilient urban planning

abstract: Technical innovations that remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere are gaining attention to compensate for the insufficient pace of emissions reductions. Given the scale of carbon dioxide removal (CDR) deployment envisioned, there is a notable deficit in our understanding of the underlying predictors of public support of CDR, particularly in the global South. In economic theory, risk, time and social preferences serve as fundamental predictors of judgment and decision making. The current article thus undertakes a systematic examination of economic preferences and how they predict support for three CDR technologies (direct air capture, enhanced rock weathering, afforestation and reforestation). We employ experimentally validated instruments to examine how fundamental differences in individual tendencies to take risks, be patient or act pro-socially affect CDR support. Drawing on nationally representative surveys in five countries (n = 4000 respondents from Brazil, China, Germany, Kenya, USA), we first establish how CDR support varies between technologies and countries, with support lower for novel CDR technologies and broadly higher for global South publics. To explain such differences, we reveal the relevance of economic preferences for CDR support, notably the positive predictive effects of risk-taking, altruism, and trust. We also indicate how the relevance of economic preferences varies across technologies and countries. Risk-taking, altruism and trust have stronger effects on novel, engineered CDR support, but positive reciprocity matters more for afforestation. The results stress the importance of economic preferences as core, under-explored predictors of individual and cross-country variation in public support of CDR technologies.

title: Risk, time and social preferences shape cross-country support for carbon dioxide removal technologies

abstract: Securities lending – the temporary transfer of securities in exchange for collateral – is essential to the modern financial system, facilitating short selling, market making, and efficient liquidity management. Yet, little is known about how these contracts are priced. Using comprehensive transaction-level data, we identify the determinants of returns from lending the same security against cash or securities collateral. We develop a model in which lending returns compensate for security risk, illiquidity, and the use of scarce dealer balance-sheet capacity. We also define a return wedge between the two market segments. Consistent with the model, the wedge widens with risk, illiquidity, dealer constraints, and collateral reusability but narrows as participation across both segments increases.
authors: Evangelos Benos & Gerardo Ferrara & Angelo Ranaldo & Vittorio Vergano
title: Price efficiency in securities lending

abstract: Hardly any study investigates the relationship between wage mobility, poverty, and inequality. Analyzing Turkish SILC data during 2006-2024, we find more wage mobility for longer time periods, particularly in the past three years. Wage mobility has largely been due to wage redistribution, rather than wage growth. Individual factors that are positively associated with higher-than-average wage mobility include working above the minimum wages, older age, having a formal job or being non-poor. Managers and professional workers or workers in large firms have most wage mobility, while workers in small to medium firms have lower-than-average to average wage mobility. Those working in the agricultural and industrial sectors have lowest wage mobility. Further regression analysis suggests that upward wage mobility and being able to maintain high wage over time are respectively associated with increases of at least 12% and 18% in poverty reduction.

abstract: We study whether immigrants' residential networks help provide them access to high-paying firms. Using Canadian longitudinal employer–employee tax data linked to immigration records, we measure employer quality with firm-specific earnings premiums and exploit variation across neighborhoods within larger locales. Neighborhood effects for immigrants operate almost entirely through immigrant-peers, not native-peers. And they are roughly twice as large when immigrant-peers share their country of birth or mother tongue. Effects arise at employer changes rather than through retention, consistent with referral and job-information channels. They nearly triple when co-resident family members are counted as peers, indicating that designs pooling household and neighborhood ties largely capture the former.
title: More than Just Neighbors: Immigrant Networks and Jobs in High-Paying Firms

abstract: Breastfeeding improves child and maternal outcomes, but it may also carry labor-market costs for mothers. This paper examines whether women hold accurate beliefs about benefits and costs of breastfeeding and whether evidence-based information can change these beliefs and breastfeeding intentions. We design and implement a survey experiment with UK women with childbearing intentions. We first elicit their prior beliefs on the effects of breastfeeding on child health, child cognitive outcomes, maternal health, and maternal labor-market outcomes. We then randomize participants to receive targeted information treatments based on existing evidence. We document substantial baseline misperceptions. Providing information leads to significant belief updating across three domains and improves belief accuracy. Treatment effects are largest among women who initially underestimated breastfeeding's effects. Information increases intended breastfeeding duration by approximately 0.67 months on average, with the strongest response among childless women, suggesting that information interventions are a potentially powerful policy tool.
title: Beliefs About Breastfeeding: Informing (Future) Mothers

abstract: Complex and opaque pay systems can weaken the link between incentives and worker behavior. We conduct a field experiment with 1,749 sewing-machine operators in Vietnam, using cross-randomized social-media videos about pay incentives. The information increases worker effort, potentially because of increased occupational self-efficacy. However, information also shifts workers toward less difficult tasks, offsetting the effort effect and leaving total output and earnings unchanged. Adding a story of a successful worker backfired and offset the effort gain. This shows that information about incentive systems must account for the multidimensionality of behavior and perceived agency at work.
title: Facts, Role Models, and Frontline Effort: Evidence from Garment Workers in Vietnam

abstract: We study whether alternative narratives about Artificial Intelligence (AI) shape workers' support for strengthening labor market policies and whether these responses differ by workplace AI use. We conduct a four-arm survey experiment on a representative sample of 2,105 Italian employees. Respondents are randomly assigned to a control group or to one of three information treatments framing AI as a technology that may substitute for human labor, complement workers' tasks, or increase the need for reskilling. We then elicit support for five labor market policies. Average treatment effects on policy support are small, but mask substantial heterogeneity by workplace AI use. Among non-users, the substitution narrative increases support for publicly funded training and hiring subsidies, while complementarity increases support for training. Among workplace AI users, both substitution and complementarity reduce support for unemployment insurance and short-time work schemes. We interpret these effects showing that, among users, the substitution narrative increases the probability of expecting household financial losses from public intervention addressing AI’s labor market effects, without a change in perceived job-loss risk.
title: Artificial Intelligence and Support for Labor Market Policies: Evidence from a Survey Experiment

abstract: The advantages of adaptive experiments have led to their rapid adoption in economics, other fields, and among practitioners. However, adaptive experiments pose challenges for causal inference. This note suggests a BOLS (batched ordinary least squares) test statistic for inference on treatment effects in adaptive experiments. The statistic provides a precision-equalizing aggregation of per-period treatment-control differences under heteroskedasticity. The combined test statistic is a linear combination of heteroskedastic per-period z-statistics and can be used to construct asymptotically valid confidence intervals. We provide simulation results comparing rejection rates in the typical case with few treatment periods and few (or many) observations per batch.
title: Inference for Batched Adaptive Experiments

abstract: This study investigates whether armed conflict deteriorates or reinvents institutional quality and function at the subnational level, employing a spatial panel econometric approach to examine Ukraine and Russia from 2010 to 2024. Using the Spatial Durbin Model, we analyze how both direct conflict exposure and spatial spillovers from neighboring regions affect institutional quality, measured through government effectiveness, regulatory quality, rule of law, and control of corruption. The results reveal three key findings. First, direct conflict exposure significantly degrades institutional quality, confirming that localized violence erodes governance capacity. Second, conflict generates substantial negative spatial spillovers, whereby instability in one region transmits institutional strain to neighboring areas. Third, institutional design conditions these effects: Ukraine's decentralized governance attenuates both direct impacts and spatial spillovers, while Russia's centralized architecture amplifies vulnerability. These findings demonstrate that the institutional consequences of war are both direct and spatially diffuse, with decentralization serving as a partial buffer against conflict-induced institutional degradation.
title: Does War Destroy Institutions or Reinvent Them? A Spatial Econometric Analysis of Regional Governance in Ukraine and Russia within the Eurasian Political Economy

abstract: College applicants in centralized systems rank programs before they know where they will be admitted and whether they will enroll and complete. We surveyed Norwegian applicants about these prospects for their first two choices after applying but before admissions and link their beliefs to administrative records. Comparing applicants just above and below admission cutoffs allows us to validate these beliefs with outcomes. Marginal applicants slightly overpredict enrollment if admitted to their first choice and underpredict it at their second, increasing between-program prediction error. While they substantially overpredict completion given enrollment for both programs, the error in the difference between programs is much smaller. In a model of applicants' rankings, correcting completion beliefs for one program changes the predicted probability of ranking the current first choice above the second by 12-14 percentage points, whereas correcting both barely changes it. Our study sheds light on validation of subjective counterfactuals and implications of their correction.
title: Getting In and Getting Through: Ex Ante Beliefs and Counterfactual Outcomes in Centralized College Admissions

abstract: Although job-hopping has become more prevalent, its implications for recruitment appear to be less favourable. Drawing on a scenario experiment with professional recruiters, this study examines the threshold at which job-hopping is penalised, the underlying perceptual mechanisms, and the factors that moderate these effects. The results indicate that substantial negative effects emerge from three prior employers within a five-year period and intensify as the number of prior employers increases. Moreover, contrary to expectations of potential benefits, job-hopping elicits exclusively negative perceptions across four theoretically derived clusters: work attitudes (perseverance, responsibility, motivation, and accuracy), career dynamics (loyalty, bore-out risk, and adaptability), human capital (past performance, in-depth experience, and willingness to learn), and social capital (team spirit, interpersonal problems, and communicative skills). Among these, the hiring penalty is most strongly associated with negative perceptions of perseverance, in-depth experience and interpersonal conflicts.
title: Quick to Quit? An Experimental Study on Employers’ Perceptions of Job-Hoppers to Explain Their Hiring Chances
